strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Interleaved Scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local scaling/unscaling operations between each all-reduce. Each iteration clones the buffer, applies per-shard scaling with division by W, reduces, then unscales. Total 8 all-reduce dispatches plus 16 local scaling passes. Matches reference implementation structure with clear separation of communication and computation phases.

strategies.name: Fused Local Operations Between Reductions
strategies.desc: Same 8 all-reduce structure but eliminates intermediate clone() calls by fusing scale/unscale operations into single vectorized kernels per stage. Pre-computes scale coefficient tensors (a[r]/W and 1/a[r]) and applies via broadcasting. Reduces to 8 all-reduce dispatches with ~14 fused local kernel launches, trading memory allocation overhead for slightly more complex indexing.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather (16 collective dispatches total). Each rank only scales its local shard between reduce-scatter and all-gather phases, reducing arithmetic operations by factor of W. Converts O(W*S) scaling loops into O(S) operations per stage, but doubles collective dispatch count from 8 to 16.

strategies.name: Batched Multi-Stage All-Reduce Pipeline
strategies.desc: Groups stages into phases (e.g., 2 groups of 4 stages) and pipelines communication by starting next all-reduce before completing local operations from previous stage where dependencies allow. Uses asynchronous all-reduce calls with manual synchronization barriers. Maintains 8 all-reduce dispatches but overlaps computation with communication for lower wall-clock time at cost of increased buffer management complexity.

strategies.name: Single-Buffer In-Place Accumulation Chain
strategies.desc:
Eliminates all clone() operations by carefully ordering in-place modifications using a single persistent buffer and temporary workspace of size W*S. Each stage writes scaled values directly to alternating buffer regions, with all-reduce operating on active region. Reduces memory traffic and allocation overhead to 8 all-reduce dispatches plus 14 in-place element-wise kernels, optimizing for memory bandwidth at world_size=224.
